defect: assert_no_future_minutes (scripts/replay_tools/runmanage.py) reads an ISO-8601 UTC offset as a clock time.
detail: the briefing field levels_at_decision_BUILD.anchored_weekly_profile.anchor holds '2026-06-22 18:00:00-04:00'. The guard's regex \b(HH):(MM)\b matches '04:00' inside the '-04:00' offset, so at a 03:00 decision it reports a future minute and REFUSES a briefing that says nothing whatever about the future.
class: FALSE POSITIVE - the guard is too strict, not too loose. It has never let a real leak through on this account.
when_it_bites: only decision minutes before 04:00, i.e. LONDON candidates between 03:00 and 03:59. That is why it never fired on day 2 (its LONDON thesis predates the check being run on theses, and every later minute has 04:00 in the past). Six of day 3's ten LONDON candidates sit in the affected band.
also_explains: several [C] items in the w49 day-1 leak audit (LONDON_0300_thesis -> 04:00, L1_0342 -> 04:00) are this same false positive, not evidence of a leak.
remedy: a local wrapper (leakcheck.py) strips ONLY a signed offset welded to the end of a timestamp - regex (?<=\d)[+-]\d\d:\d\d - then runs the unmodified repo guard. A bare '04:00' in prose, a time after a space, and the whole forward-phrase blacklist are all untouched.
